reviewers.summary: The passcode step exposes the seeded-user picker without validating the passcode, and the sign-in request omits the required anti-forgery header. The tests do not catch either defect.

findingList.message: The seeded-user picker is shown without validating the passcode, contrary to the first acceptance criterion. This exposes user metadata before the sign-in gate (OWASP A01:2025).

evidence.codePathTraced: continueWithPasscode checks only that the passcode is nonempty, then fetches /api/auth/users without sending or validating it and displays the returned users.
evidence.failureScenario: A visitor enters an incorrect passcode; if /api/auth/users returns the seeded users, the picker appears before any successful passcode step, exposing the roster.

findingList.message: The sign-in POST omits the required anti-forgery header, despite the criterion requiring it on every state-changing request.

evidence.codePathTraced: signIn sends a state-changing POST to /api/auth/sign-in with only a Content-Type header; it has no anti-forgery token.
evidence.failureScenario: When the server requires the specified anti-forgery header, submitting the sign-in form sends no token and the request is rejected (OWASP A01:2025).

findingList.message: The tests do not verify that an incorrect passcode keeps the seeded-user picker hidden, as required by the first acceptance criterion.

evidence.codePathTraced: The passcode-step test enters a nonempty value and checks that users appear; the wrong-passcode test reaches the picker before submitting sign-in.
evidence.failureScenario: If any nonempty passcode reveals the picker, these tests still pass, so the first acceptance criterion's successful-passcode gate is unverified.

findingList.message: The tests do not verify the anti-forgery header on sign-in, leaving the second acceptance criterion's requirement for every state-changing request untested.

evidence.codePathTraced: The anti-forgery test checks the sign-out request header; no test checks the sign-in request header.
evidence.failureScenario: If the sign-in POST omits its required anti-forgery header, the current tests still pass because the header assertion covers only sign-out.

reviewers.summary: The passcode step reveals the seeded-user picker before validating the passcode, and the sign-in request omits the required anti-forgery header. Both behaviors violate the acceptance criteria.

findingList.message: The seeded-user picker appears without validating the passcode, contrary to the first acceptance criterion. This exposes user information before the sign-in gate (OWASP A01:2025).

evidence.codePathTraced: continueWithPasscode checks only that the passcode is nonempty, then fetches /api/auth/users and displays the returned users without validating the passcode.
evidence.failureScenario: An unauthenticated visitor enters an incorrect nonempty passcode; if /api/auth/users returns the seeded users, the picker reveals their names and roles before any successful passcode step.

findingList.message: The sign-in POST omits the required anti-forgery header, despite the criterion requiring it on every state-changing request (OWASP A01:2025).

evidence.codePathTraced: signIn sends a state-changing POST to /api/auth/sign-in with only a Content-Type header; it does not send the required anti-forgery token.
evidence.failureScenario: When the server requires the specified anti-forgery header, submitting the sign-in form sends no token and the request is rejected. The tests check the sign-out header but do not catch this omission.

reviewers.summary: The passcode step reveals seeded-user data without validating the passcode, and the sign-in POST lacks the required anti-forgery header.

findingList.message: The seeded-user roster can be disclosed before passcode validation, contrary to the first acceptance criterion (OWASP A01:2025 Broken Access Control).

evidence.codePathTraced: The passcode handler checks only that the field is nonempty, then fetches /api/auth/users without sending or validating the passcode and displays the response.
evidence.failureScenario: An unauthenticated visitor enters any nonempty value; if the endpoint returns the seeded users, the visitor sees their names and roles without passing the required sign-in step.

findingList.message: The sign-in request omits the required anti-forgery token header (OWASP A01:2025 Broken Access Control).

evidence.codePathTraced: The state-changing POST to /api/auth/sign-in sends only Content-Type; the anti-forgery token is not included.
evidence.failureScenario: When the server requires its specified anti-forgery header, submitting the sign-in form omits it and the server rejects the request, preventing sign-in.
